summary: For each index return the product of all other elements, without using division.
mainInsight: Product except self = (product of everything to the left) x (product of everything to the right). Precompute prefix and suffix products so no division is needed and zeros cause no trouble.

approaches.name: Brute force
approaches.summary: For each i multiply all other elements.

approaches.name: Prefix and suffix arrays
approaches.summary: prefix[i] * suffix[i+1] computed from two passes.

approaches.name: Prefix pass + running suffix
approaches.summary: Write prefix products into the output, then multiply by a running suffix from the right.

personalSolution.notes: Optimal time. Improve space to O(1) extra by reusing the output array and a running suffix variable; also avoid mutating the input.

promptVariants: Which technique solves Product Except Self in O(n) without division?
What pattern fits 'combine everything to the left and right of i'?
cards.explanation: The product excluding i factors into left-product x right-product, each computable cumulatively.

incorrectOptionExplanations.Sliding window: No contiguous window is being maintained.

promptVariants: Why do prefix and suffix products avoid division and handle zeros?
Explain the factorisation behind the solution.
cards.answer: answer[i] = (nums[0..i-1] product) x (nums[i+1..n-1] product). Both partial products are built cumulatively with multiplication only, so zeros simply propagate to the correct positions instead of causing divide-by-zero.
cards.explanation: Division would fail or need special zero cases.

promptVariants: In your prefix array, what does prefix[i] represent?
Define prefix[i] and suffix[i] in your solution.
cards.answer: prefix[i] is the product of the first i elements (indices 0..i-1); suffix[i] is the product of the last i elements. Thus answer[i] = prefix[i] * suffix[n-1-i].
keyPoints: prefix[i] = product of first i elements
cards.explanation: The leading 1 is the empty product.

promptVariants: Product Except Self runs in ___ time with prefix/suffix products.
How can the extra space be reduced from O(n) to O(1)?
What is the follow-up trick to get O(1) extra space for Product Except Self?
cards.answer: Store prefix products directly in the output array, then sweep from the right keeping a running suffix product and multiply it into the output. Only a couple of scalars are extra.
cards.explanation: This is the follow-up the problem statement hints at.

promptVariants: Why is the answer `prefix[i] * suffix[n - i - 1]` and not `suffix[i]`?
Explain the index arithmetic suffix[n - i - 1] in the final loop.
cards.answer: suffix was built from the right end, so suffix[j] is the product of the last j elements. The elements to the right of i are the last n-1-i elements, hence suffix[n-1-i]. Also note this overwrites nums, mutating the caller's input.
keyPoints: Right of i = last n-1-i elements
cards.explanation: Prefix of length i covers elements before i.

promptVariants: For nums = [1,2,0,4] what does the answer look like?
How do two zeros affect the output?
cards.explanation: Only index 2 (the zero) excludes the zero factor: 1*2*4 = 8; every other index multiplies by 0. With two zeros the whole output is 0.

incorrectOptionExplanations.[0,0,0,0]: That is the result with two zeros, not one.
incorrectOptionExplanations.[8,4,0,2]: Division by the total would give nonsense here.
incorrectOptionExplanations.[24,12,0,6]: Wrong: that ignores the zero element.

canonicalCode:
class Solution:
    def productExceptSelf(self, nums: List[int]) -> List[int]:
        n = len(nums)
        out = [1] * n
        prefix = 1
        for i in range(n):                       # out[i] = product of everything left of i
            out[i] = prefix
            prefix *= nums[i]
        suffix = 1
        for i in range(n - 1, -1, -1):           # multiply by the product right of i
            out[i] *= suffix
            suffix *= nums[i]
        return out
